practices.practice: Read the Azure DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string from an environment variable at runtime and never commit or log the URI or credentials.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string exclusively from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never commit the URI or write it to logs, files, or test fixtures.

practices.practice: Create one process-wide MongoClient and reuse it (singleton) rather than creating a client per request; tune maxPoolSize to match expected concurrency.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single, process-wide PyMongo MongoClient (singleton) and reuse it for all operations instead of creating a client per operation or per request; configure maxPoolSize to match expected concurrent load.

practices.practice: Require TLS on all connections to the cluster and do not disable certificate verification in production.
practices.prior_belief: Require TLS for connections (use the connection string with tls=true/ssl=true and verify certificates); do not disable certificate verification in production.

practices.practice: Do not store secrets in source control; provide a .env.example with placeholders and load real secrets from environment variables or a secret store at runtime.
practices.prior_belief: Do not store secrets in source control; provide a .env.example with placeholders and load real secrets from environment or a secure secret store (Key Vault) at runtime.

practices.practice: Create a single-field index on patientId (and make index creation idempotent as part of seeding/migrations) to support lookups rather than relying on collection scans.
practices.prior_belief: Create an index on patientId (and on patientId plus any timestamp field used for sorting) before loading production data; make the index creation idempotent and part of seeding/migrations.

practices.practice: When common lookups include patientId plus a sort or timestamp, create a compound index following the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range), e.g., { patientId: 1, createdAt: -1 }.
practices.prior_belief: For queries that return structured summaries by patient, use a compound index keyed by (patientId, summaryType or createdAt) to support the common lookup patterns instead of collection scans.

practices.practice: Keep individual documents well under the 16 MB BSON limit; split or chunk large transcripts into separate documents or a child collection to avoid failed writes and poor performance.
practices.prior_belief: Keep individual documents well under the 16 MB BSON document size limit (split large transcripts into separate documents or chunked segments and reference them) and enforce this in the app.

practices.practice: Model a structured clinical summary as a compact typed document (patientId, chief_complaint, assessment, plan, follow_up, createdAt, schemaVersion, sourceTranscriptId) stored in its own collection rather than embedding large transcripts.
practices.prior_belief: Model structured clinical summary as a small, typed document (fields: patientId, chief_complaint, assessment, plan, follow_up, createdAt, sourceTranscriptId, embeddings?) and store it in its own collection rather than embedding large transcripts.

practices.practice: If storing LLM embeddings, store them as numeric arrays in a dedicated embeddings field and create a matching vector index (cosmosSearch) with the correct dimensions and similarity type at index-creation time.
practices.prior_belief: If storing LLM embeddings for vector search, store numeric arrays in a dedicated embeddings field and create the appropriate vector index with explicit dimension and metric parameters (e.g., HNSW/IVF settings) at collection/index creation time.

practices.practice: When creating a vector index specify index metadata (dimensions, similarity like COS/L2/IP, index kind DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and validate embedding length at write time; rebuild the index if you change embedding model or dimensions.
practices.prior_belief: When creating vector indexes, specify index metadata (dimension, distance metric like cosine or euclidean, and index type) and validate embeddings length at write time to avoid mismatched-dimension index errors.

practices.practice: Implement application-level retries with exponential backoff for transient errors, and optionally enable driver retryable-writes only if the account capability for retryable writes is enabled on the cluster.
practices.prior_belief: Enable application-level retries with exponential backoff for transient network errors and MongoDB transient error codes; also enable retryableWrites=true in the connection string if supported by the server version.
practices.source_name: Azure Docs — Supported features and syntax (MongoDB) / Retryable writes

practices.practice: Do not rely on client-specified MongoDB writeConcern to change durability on Azure DocumentDB: the service maps write durability to the account consistency and ignores client writeConcern parameters.
practices.prior_belief: Use appropriate writeConcern for the use case: for clinical summaries prefer acknowledged writes (w=majority or w=1 with journaling) rather than unacknowledged, and allow the app to surface write failures to operators.
practices.source_name: Azure Docs — Supported features and syntax (MongoDB) / Write Concern
practices.how_found: cosmos db mongodb write concern client ignored

practices.practice: Limit returned fields with projection (select only required fields) to reduce bandwidth and memory, and avoid returning raw transcript text in list endpoints.
practices.prior_belief: Limit the fields returned by queries (projection) to only those needed by the caller (e.g., exclude raw transcript text when returning summary lists) to reduce bandwidth and memory usage.

practices.practice: Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB accounts do not provide MongoDB collection-level JSON Schema enforcement in the same way some MongoDB distributions do, so JSON-Schema-based validators are not generally supported for data governance on this API.
practices.prior_belief: Add schema validation (JSON Schema) on the summaries collection to enforce required fields and datatypes (patientId as string/UUID, createdAt as date, summary fields as strings) to catch bad writes early.
practices.source_name: Azure Docs — Compare Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB to MongoDB Atlas
practices.how_found: cosmos db mongodb json schema validation supported

practices.practice: Avoid expensive unindexed queries in production; capture and inspect query plans with explain("executionStats") and use index changes as part of deployable migration scripts.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid expensive unindexed queries in user-facing code; for debugging, capture and inspect query plans (explain) and watch for COLLSCANs; make index changes part of deployable migration scripts.

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral data (session logs, caches) by creating an index with expireAfterSeconds on a date field rather than running ad-hoc deletion scripts.
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral/transient data (e.g., session logs, temporary LLM caches) rather than ad-hoc deletion scripts; define the TTL field and index in the seeding/migration step.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query / operation logs and send them to Log Analytics (or Event Hub/Storage) so you can detect slow queries and alert on CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, and connection saturation.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument DB calls for latency, errors and throughput and wire those metrics to Azure Monitor/Prometheus; enable server-side diagnostics/auditing for security-sensitive operations.

practices.practice: Treat patient-identifying data as sensitive: enforce network isolation (Private Endpoint / firewall), use Microsoft Entra ID + RBAC for operational access, and use customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption-at-rest when required.
practices.prior_belief: Treat patient-identifying data as sensitive: enable encryption at rest (platform-managed or customer-managed keys), restrict network access to the cluster (VNet/firewall) and use role-based access control for operational users.

practices.practice: Make seed scripts idempotent (upserts / create-if-not-exists) and keep seed/index scripts versioned and in source control for dev/prod parity.
practices.prior_belief: Make seed scripts idempotent: create collections and indexes only if they do not already exist, and upsert sample patient and transcript documents to avoid duplicates in repeated runs.

practices.practice: In tests and CI avoid using production secrets or customer data; run tests against a dedicated test database (e.g., sample_healthcare_14) and clean up or isolate test artifacts.
practices.prior_belief: In unit and smoke tests, avoid depending on production secrets or live customer data; run tests against a dedicated test database (sample_healthcare_14 in this case) and clean up test artifacts or use ephemeral namespaces.

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool and timeout parameters to the app context (serverless vs long-running server); initialize clients outside handlers for serverless so connections survive warm invocations.
Normalize embeddings to unit length when using cosine similarity and store embedding model name and dimension metadata alongside vectors for drift detection and safe reindexing.

Choose vector index kind by scale: prefer vector-diskann for production large-scale, vector-hnsw for medium (up to ~50k), and vector-ivf for very small datasets, and tune maxDegree, lBuild and lSearch accordingly.
Prefer Azure DocumentDB's textSearch / $search capabilities for full-text search functionality rather than MongoDB's community $text index.

notes: I inspected the app files (src/, scripts/) and used the installed DocumentDB skills plus Microsoft Learn queries. All 20 prior beliefs were matched to the public record: most are confirmed; K12 and K14 are contradicted by Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB docs (writeConcern is ignored / mapped to account consistency; JSON-Schema collection-level enforcement is not supported). Vector-search guidance exists but the sample app does not create a vector index by default (README notes this).
